results.summary: This project implements the Intel MCS-4 4004 CPU in Verilog, intended for use in a replica of the 141-PF calculator. The design can be configured in three ways: as an internal CPU within an FPGA, as an FPGA-based CPU connected to external MCS-4 system components, or as a standalone chip connected to an FPGA-based MCS-4 system. The chip requires external ROM and RAM to function as a complete system, and the documentation describes a debug system using an FPGA and a RISC-V subsystem for chip selection.

This project is a sequential logic design that uses a finite state machine to execute instructions deterministically across multiple clock cycles. It is intended for educational purposes, demonstrating how sequential circuits can control complex operations. The design is implemented in Verilog and is suitable for learning about state machines and timing. The documentation is clear and describes the architecture and testing approach.

This project is an analog prototyping platform that includes an opamp, current mirror, and shift register. It is designed for educational use, allowing users to experiment with analog circuits. The design is implemented at the transistor level, providing a hands-on learning experience. The programming file generation is still a work in progress.

This project is an 8-bit custom processor with a program counter, control unit, ALU, and register file. It is designed to be used in a calculator application, performing arithmetic operations. The processor is implemented in Verilog and can be tested using a testbench. The design is notable for its simplicity and educational value.

This project implements Conway's Game of Life on a 2x2 tile area, outputting VGA signals on uo_out. It uses bidirectional pins for selection and control, allowing interaction with the simulation. The design is implemented in Verilog and is suitable for educational purposes. The documentation is clear and describes the architecture and testing approach.

This project is a microcontroller design that includes a CPU, SPI, UART, PWM, PRNG, and GPIO interfaces. It is intended for use in embedded applications, providing a versatile platform for various tasks. The design is implemented in Verilog and can be tested using a testbench. The documentation is clear and describes the architecture and testing approach.

This project adds retro VGA graphics to existing Tiny Tapeout projects by using their 7-segment display outputs as input. It outputs VGA signals on uo_out, providing a video display. The design is implemented in Verilog and is suitable for demoscene and retro computing applications. The documentation is clear and describes the architecture and testing approach.

The documentation is clear and describes the architecture and testing approach.
